text:
alice: quick note — eu-west1 GPUPool is showing sustained queue growth for the past ~2 hours. tokens (TPM) accounting looks off vs actual GPU time.

bob: can you paste the metrics? TPM consumed vs refill?

alice: graphs: queue_length + avg_gpu_time per request spiked after the midnight deploy. TPM burn rate >> configured refill. looks like long-chat sessions holding KV caches and doing slow reranks.

carlos: interesting — are we charging tokens at arrival or at completion? last I checked we bill arrival with estimated tokens, which undercounts streaming + rerank overhead.

alice: arrival. that creates a smear: small requests with post-init reranks keep occupying GPU but we've already debited their TPM, so admission lets more in and we hit GPU concurrency limits.

dana: so admission controller thinks we have capacity but GPUs are saturated. we need a conservative quick fix: change admission to reserve an extra safety margin for long-tail ops. maybe a 15% buffer for chat models.

emily: long-term we probably want to switch to a two-phase accounting: reserve tokens at arrival+predictive extra for expected KV/steady-state duration, then reconcile at completion. but that's a fair amount of infra work.

bob: for emergency, can we enable burst-credit gating per pool? reduce per-pool burst tokens from 300 -> 100 and lower burst window. that'll throttle sudden oversubscribe.

alice: +1. also enabling regional fallback is fine but we still want predictable SLA for dedicated customers.

ops-bot: [alert] eu-west1: GPUPool saturation > 90% (5m avg). queue_length=184, active_requests=240, tpm_burn_rate=16200/min.

carlos: quick calc: current config: pool_capacity_tokens=12000/min, burst=300, refill_period=60s. Observed burn 16200 => oversubscribe 35% -> queue. If we enforce admission: allowed_tpm = pool_capacity_tokens * (1 - safety_margin). With 15% safety_margin allowed_tpm=10200.

alice: can we push a temporary admission rule? example override in k8s config:

```
kind: AdmissionConfig
metadata:
  name: eu-west1-emergency
spec:
  token_policy: conservative
  safety_margin: 0.15
  burst_limit: 100
  reconcile_at_completion: false
```

bob: I can roll that out to eu-west1 in the next 5m. will monitor queue.

dana: also add a metric we can alert on: token_discrepancy = tpm_debited_at_arrival - effective_gpu_tokens_used (5m EWMA). alert when > 15% for 10m.

emily: adding to roadmap: implement completion-based reconciliation + predictive reserve model using observed session_length_histogram and model_kv_factor. ETA 2 sprints.

alice: logs for one offending request (shortened):
```
req=abcd1234 model=gpt-redwood-chat v=2026-02-15 tokens_est=128 tokens_debited=128 start=12:03:01 gpu_acquire=12:03:02 gpu_release=12:05:40 post_rerank=12:06:10
```

alice: this shows GPU held ~158s but we only debited ~128 tokens at arrival. mismatch.

carlos: ok. for next deploy we should: 1) add small extra debit factor for models with >P95 session length, 2) instrument effective_gpu_token_seconds metric, 3) add admission safety_margin toggle per customer tier.

bob: rolled emergency override to eu-west1; burst_limit -> 100, safety_margin -> 0.15. monitoring now.

ops-bot: [info] rollout eu-west1-emergency applied by bob at 1982468220.

alice: thx. let's keep this thread updated with the alert status and follow up with a short postmortem next week on accounting semantics. :thumbsup:
